note: The Kingdom of the Netherlands' common visa list for its Caribbean parts (Aruba, Curaçao, Sint Maarten, and Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba): nationals of the countries listed enter without a visa for 90 days in any 180, US nationals for 180 in any 365; everyone else needs a Caribbean visa. Hong Kong's and Macao's exemption is for SAR passports, Taiwan's for passports with the identity card number, Ukraine's for biometric passports. Dutch nationals are taken as home (the right of abode there is limited to those with a connection to the island, others staying 180 days in 365: not modelled). Holders of a Schengen multiple-entry visa or residence, a UK or Irish multiple-entry visa or residence, a US or Canadian residence, or a French overseas residence need no Caribbean visa (not modelled). The territories' differences are each one's own rules on top.

sources.title: NetherlandsWorldwide (Government of the Netherlands), Do I need a visa for the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom?
sources.said: You can travel to the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom (Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Saba, St Eustatius and St Maarten) without a visa if any of the following applies to you. ... You do not need a visa if you are a national of 1 of the following countries: Albania Andorra Antigua and Barbuda Argentina Australia Austria Bahamas Barbados Belgium Belize Bosnia and Herzegovina Brazil Brunei Darussalam Bulgaria Canada Chile Colombia Costa Rica Croatia Cyprus Czech Republic Denmark Dominica Ecuador El Salvador Estonia Finland France Germany Greece Grenada Guatemala Guyana: You do need a visa for St Maarten. Honduras Hong Kong: You do not need a visa if you have a British National Overseas passport or a Special Administrative Region passport. Hungary Iceland Ireland Israel Italy Jamaica: Curaçao only. You do need a visa for the other Caribbean parts of the Kingdom. Japan Latvia Liechtenstein Lithuania Luxembourg Macao: You do not need a visa if you have a Special Administrative Region passport. Malaysia Malta Mauritius Mexico Moldova Monaco Montenegro Netherlands New Zealand Nicaragua North Macedonia Norway Panama Paraguay Peru Poland Portugal Romania San Marino Serbia Seychelles Singapore Slovakia Slovenia South Korea Spain St Kitts and Nevis St Lucia St Vincent and the Grenadines Suriname Sweden Switzerland Taiwan: You do not need a visa if you have passport bearing your identity card number. Trinidad and Tobago Ukraine: You do not need a visa if you have a biometric passport. United Arab Emirates United Kingdom United States of America Uruguay Vatican City

sources.title: NetherlandsWorldwide (Government of the Netherlands), What are the requirements for travelling to the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom without a visa?
sources.said: If you do not need a visa to travel to the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom, you may stay there for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period. If you are a Dutch or US national, you can stay for longer: a maximum of 180 consecutive days in any 365-day period.
